notes: Part D omitted — this exercise forbade opening any reading. Answered strictly from documented biography (Wikipedia, BBC, UPI wire archives 1987, Rolling Stone, The Conversation, davidbowie.com, The Bowie Bible, Billboard, Sotheby's/Warner Chappell reporting), with no astrological source consulted at any point. Born David Robert Jones, 8 Jan 1947, at the family home, 40 Stansfield Road, Brixton, London — hence B5=home. A1/A2/A3: England and Wales birth certificates do not record time of birth for singletons, so no certificate time exists; the only widely circulated figure is a round hour, which is why A2=round_hour and A1/A3=unknown rather than a guessed provenance. A4/A5: documented admissions are Feb 1962 (Farnborough Hospital then Moorfields Eye Hospital, emergency operation after George Underwood's punch scratched the eyeball; sources differ between two months' recovery and four months of treatment/'operations' plural) and June 2004 (heart attack onstage in Prague / Hamburg, emergency angioplasty for a blocked artery); chemotherapy 2014–2016 for liver cancer probably makes the true count four_plus, but 'two_three' is what is firmly documented. A tabloid-sourced claim of 'six heart attacks' is not reliably corroborated and was not used. A6: eyes (permanent anisocoria and impaired depth perception from 1962), heart (2004), liver (hepatocellular cancer diagnosed mid-2014, inoperable Nov 2015, died 10 Jan 2016), nerves (documented cocaine-driven insomnia, paranoia and psychosis 1974–76); heavy lifelong smoking is documented but no recurring chest/lung diagnosis is, so chest_lungs was left off. A7/A8/A9 genuinely thin: no childhood illness or near-death is recorded and no grandparent lifespans could be found, so 'average'/'no'/'unknown'. A10/A11: John Jones (Barnardo's press officer, steady salaried work through the 1950s) bought David his first saxophone in 1961, brought home the American 45s that started him, and helped connect him with manager Kenneth Pitt — supportive; he died of pneumonia 5 Aug 1969, weeks after 'Space Oddity', Bowie saying he 'died at the wrong damn time'. A12: Peggy Jones is described by biographers as undemonstrative and emotionally distant, with a public rift in the mid-1980s over Terry; 'distant' chosen over 'conflicted' because that is the better-sourced characterisation. She died in 2001 (April, per the standard chronology — date is the least certain item in B6). A13: half-brother Terry Burns (b. 1937), the formative influence of his youth, was diagnosed schizophrenic, institutionalised at Cane Hill and died by suicide at Coulsdon South station on 16 Jan 1985 — 'lost' is the only fitting option; half-sister Annette (b. 1941) makes him the youngest of the sibling set (B4=youngest) though he was his parents' only joint child. A14/A15: left Bromley Technical High School July 1963 with one GCE O level in Art; the 1962 eye injury cost him roughly two months of school, hence 'brief'; the 1999 Berklee doctorate is honorary and does not count as completed education. A16/A17: one four-to-five-month salaried job (junior visualiser at Nevin D. Hirst Advertising, 1963, which he 'loathed'), everything afterwards self-directed and self-owned. A18: astrology_occult is selected on documented biography only — Tibetan Buddhism under Chime Rinpoche in 1967, Kabbalah and occult obsession during Station to Station — not from any chart. A21: no documented gambling or lottery; 'net_gain' reflects the 1997 $55m Bowie-Bonds securitisation, the $17m EMI deal, and an art collection that fetched £32.9m at Sotheby's in 2016. A22: no inheritance or windfall is on record, which also makes C4 a low-confidence call. A23: in July 1975 he discovered the MainMan terms left him with nothing and roughly half a million dollars in debt — serious trouble, later fully resolved. A24–A27: married Angela Barnett March 1970, divorced Feb 1980 (she surrendered custody of Duncan); married Iman 24 April 1992 (Lausanne, solemnised Florence 6 June) and remained married until his death, a partnership uniformly described as happy — A25 gives the first marriage year per the template's convention. A28: two children, Duncan Zowie Haywood Jones (30 May 1971) and Alexandria 'Lexi' Zahra Jones (15 Aug 2000). A31: 'extended' rests on the documented 1974–76 cocaine psychosis and paranoia, his own 1993 Arena account of fearing inherited insanity (three maternal aunts and Terry affected), and later alcohol problems; formal psychiatric treatment is not documented. A34: hospital stays only, no institutional confinement. A35 omits, for space, the 1953 family move to Bromley, the 1963 first job (captured in B6), the July 1975 MainMan debt discovery, and the 1983 Let's Dance commercial peak. A36 is unanswerable as posed — he died 10 Jan 2016 — so 'same' is entered as the null option; posthumously the period does include the Jan 2022 $250m Warner Chappell catalogue sale and the 2023 V&A archive gift. B1=opt1 because 'hates show' is disqualifying for the most theatrical performer of his generation and he was famously guarded and strategic offstage ('quite content spending days without saying a word to anybody'), even though the 'philosophy and hidden subjects' half of opt2 does fit. B3=younger is a documented commonplace about his appearance rather than a hard fact. Legal history considered: the March 1976 Rochester NY felony marijuana arrest (grand jury refused to indict) and the Oct 1987 Dallas sexual-assault allegation by Wanda Nichols (no-billed by a Dallas County grand jury, 18 Nov 1987); he refused a CBE (2000) and a knighthood (2003) but accepted French Commandeur des Arts et des Lettres. C11=opt1 reflects the Kenneth Pitt and Tony Defries management disasters, the RCA falling-out, and his loathing of his only nine-to-five. C9=opt1 reflects a career built on discarding personas, styles, addictions and countries.
